newsitem.title: USA: Pharmacia & Upjohn arthritis drug cleared by FDA.
newsitem.headline: Pharmacia & Upjohn arthritis drug cleared by FDA.

text.p: Pharmacia & Upjohn said Monday it received clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to sell Azulfidine EN-tabs Tablets for treatment of rheumatoid arthritis.
The drug is for patients who have not responded adequately to, or are intolerant of, analgesics or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs.

Azulfidine EN-tabs are coated to reduce stomach absorption and minimize gastrointestinal irritation. The tabs have been available for treatment of rheumatoid arthritis in 43 countries. They have also been available in the United States for treatment of ulcerative colitis.

About 2.5 million Americans suffer from rheumatoid arthritis. Patients with active forms of the disease have a 70 percent probablity of developing joint damage within two years of the disease's onset.
Pharmacia said many of those patients may require additional treatment if traditional non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs were inadequate.
Clinical tests of Azulfidine EN-tabs showed dbout a third of participants suffered side effects, including anorexia, headaches, nausea, vomiting, gastric distress and reversible low sperm count.
The scientific name for the drug is sulfasalazine delayed-release tablet.
